overview_markdown:
KafClaw is an enterprise-oriented multi-agent coordination framework written in Go, using Apache Kafka as its messaging backbone. Rather than a single local assistant like OpenClaw, it targets distributed agent swarms: agents communicate through a structured topic hierarchy (`group.<name>.requests`, `.responses`, `.traces`, `.control.*`) with typed envelopes for announce, request, response, trace, memory, and audit messages, each carrying correlation IDs and timestamps for built-in observability.

Its core contributions include hierarchical orchestration, shared memory, distributed skill routing, and an agent onboarding protocol — all decoupled from any specific LLM provider or runtime. It is part of a broader Scalytics-backed platform suite (KafScale, GitClaw, Scalytics Copilot), positioning it as infrastructure for private, self-hosted AI operations rather than a consumer assistant.

Compared to OpenClaw, KafClaw trades approachability for scale: it demands Kafka operational expertise and has a tiny community (21 stars), but offers audit-grade tracing and multi-agent coordination that OpenClaw's local-first model doesn't target. Recent activity is healthy, with a v1.0.0 release, CodeQL scanning, fuzz/smoke CI, and steady dependency maintenance.
